newsitem.title: CHINA: China's shares end up on buying in blue-chips.
newsitem.headline: China's shares end up on buying in blue-chips.

text.p: China's A and B share indices ended higher across the board on Wednesday on selective buying of blue-chips, which are expected to post strong results for 1996, brokers said.
But trading volumes in Shanghai were thin with institutions sidelined ahead of the release of results, they said. All firms are required to issue 1996 results before April 30.
Shanghai's B index inched up 0.435 points or 0.66 percent to 66.731 points on volume of 14.68 million shares worth $7.03 million, down from $8.39 million on Tuesday.
The A share index closed up 14.374 points or 1.35 percent to 1,078.204 points on volume of 573.7 million shares worth 5.9 billion yuan.
"Individual buying in counters expected to post good 1996 results pushed the index up," said one broker.
Another broker said institutional investors had little interest in building positions due to uncertainty over results.

On the B share market, building material maker Shanghai Huili was the star on speculative buying, rising $0.012 or 4.76 percent to $0.264 on volume of 179,000 shares. Blue-chip Shanghai Refrigerator Compressor traded the most on anticipation of good 1996 results, gaining $0.024 or 4.49 percent to $0.558 on volume of 2.1 million shares.
On the A share market, the SSE30 index rose 14.374 points or 1.35 percent to 2,811.623 points.
Clothing maker Kangsai was the star on the release of good annual results, jumping 2.13 yuan or 10.00 percent to 23.43 yuan on volume of 700,100 shares.
Shenzhen's B share index gained 0.87 points or 0.58 percent to 151.74 on turnover of HK$97 million, up from HK$85 million on Tuesday.
The A share index rose 8.69 points or 2.36 percent to 377.40, with turnover swelling to 7.40 billion yuan from 6.35 billion.

"Prices rose on investors' optimism over China's economy, given Beijing's decision to keep retail price inflation below six percent in 1997," said Song Bin, an analyst with Central-South Securities Co said.
"Investors increased their positions in counters expected to post good 1996 results," he said. "But the market is slightly over-bought, so there is some profit-taking looming."
"The impact of Deng Xiaoping's death on the stock market has faded away with his funeral ceremony on Tuesday," another broker added.
On the B share market, refrigerator maker Hefei Meilin was the most active and best performing counter. It rose HK$0.22 or 3.62 percent to HK$6.30 on volume of 3.13 million shares.
Chengdu Taikang Chemical Fibre Co debuted on Shenzhen's A share market with a listing of 27.30 million shares, ending the session at 11.08 yuan.
